paras: Induction: gathering attention without disappearing

Why an induction? The job of an induction is to bring your attention together so that you can hear the stuff that is waiting for you in the quiet spaces. This is not a time for giving in, for playing as if you were asleep, or for obeying anybody. If you are feeling sober, distracted, analytical, or closed in some way, you might want to do an actual induction. If, on the other hand, you are already feeling trancey, from meditation, or from loveyhuasca, or from lucid dreaming, or from grief, or from music, or from prayer, or from not having slept, or whatever, skip straight to the orientation and containment part.
You need just enough trance to feel focused, warm, receptive, embodied, and able to stop what you're doing if you want to. Beyond that, it is entirely optional.
What an induction is actually doing

It prepares you for what is to come, by gathering your attention to a point where you can deepen your experience. Some inductions are more flexible than others, allowing you to change them to match what is happening to you as you go along. Others, like counting, are fixed. There are lots of ways of gathering your attention. You don't even need an induction, if you are honest about what you are doing.

If you have a very simple target you can try out some suggestions before deepening, and if they work you can deepen from that. However, there are ways of getting your attention that don't require a full ceremony.
Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance

Pick something. Pick why you are doing it, pick an anchor, pick an image, pick how you will get back again. Then keep that in mind and decide if you want it to be warm or boundaried, if you want it to have a direction or not, if you want it to be neutral or not. Floating, stairways, gardens, inner spaces, colours, talking to an inner child etc. are all handy. Just pick one, and if you change it, do it consciously.

You don't have to use images. You can use sensations, rhythms, movements, words, spatial information, simple knowing or even not responding at all to indicate that you have received a signal. If you make up your own induction words, keep the language consistent. If you are counting, give it some meaning. If you are going somewhere, come back again. You can borrow some of the qualities of whatever you are talking about, but don't lose yourself.

Pick a verb to use as central, a sensory quality to associate, a few words as a refrain, and a phrase to use to move from one thing to another. Read the induction out loud to yourself, and remember that long elegant sentences become soup when you are inducted.
Before you begin

Read this and the Come all the way back bit in full, when you are completely awake. Pick something to do. Pick what you want to explore or what quality you want to invite in. Pick what you will not be exploring. Make some time for it. Remember that it is okay to use hypnosis for love, play, confidence, creativity, communion etc. as well as to explore other things. Make sure you leave enough time to come back and think about what you have done.

Make sure you are somewhere where you can be physically safe. Don't drive, go in the water, play with machinery, look after other people etc. while you are in there. If you are intoxicated, confused or otherwise not able to be physically safe, don't do this. Just deal with the issue of getting you some immediate support instead. (NB The Already open? bit later on doesn't count - it's meant to orient you, not to make things worse.)

Decide how you want to be encouraged, and let yourself know what is going to happen, especially if you are going to close your eyes or come out and go in again. If possible, read this before you listen to it. If you are recording this, it is okay to read it over before you start, even if you don't read it as you go along. Give yourself a word for stopping, just in case you need it. Any word will do, but 'stop' is a good one. It's also a good idea to have a word for turning it down, like 'less'. If you want to turn the words off, use 'quiet'. It is always okay to open your eyes and stop doing this. Even if some part of you doesn't want you to.

If you haven't done this sort of thing before, rehearse going in and coming out again until it feels easy. You don't have to keep an eye on it all the time. You are only asking your body and mind to do something that they are already capable of, in a way that requires less work from you. Saying no means no. It is not okay for me, or any other internal voice, to talk to you without your permission.

Remember to use utilization - to let what happens next be informed by how you responded to what happened last time. You can learn some more about this in Appendix B , and how to use it after the induction in Let the next response guide you . Until then, just keep an eye open for what is actually happening. Don't assume that because nothing seems to be happening that you have succeeded in secret. Keep all the safety and exiting instructions straightforward.
Sober induction (3 - 5 minutes)
Sober induction: 3–5 minutes

Read this slowly into a tape recorder, or read it out loud to yourself, or use it silently if you are that good. Pick an anchor (sound, touch, two hand practice etc.) and say the first bit over and over again, using the same anchor every time. Don't read the bits between the paragraphs out loud, but do pause for a little while.
1) Begin by looking, not to see anything in particular, but to allow your eyes to focus on something in the room.

2) Now, as you continue, turn your attention to the surface you are and notice what it feels like to be in contact with that surface. You may wish to switch to an ambient sound, or your breathing, if you prefer.
3) You might wish to take some time with this...
4) If you wish, you may notice any thoughts that may still be present in your mind, and then return your attention to your chosen anchoring point...
5) You might wish to focus in on some particular aspect of what you are seeing, or hearing, or feeling, or simply the act of listening, or seeing, or feeling itself...
6) You might wish to take some time to listen to what you have to say to yourself...
7) Now, bring to mind your chosen phrase, and receive it as best you can...

8) You may wish to close your eyes now, or soften your gaze, or continue with your eyes open... Continue to listen, if you wish, to the sound of these words as a background to whatever you wish to do now...
9) In a moment, I will count from 5 to 1...
10) 5.. Notice again your chosen anchor point.. 4.. Gather up your attention.. 3.. 2.. 1..
11) Now bring to mind, if you wish, whatever it is you wish to make contact with, or simply allow yourself to be in contact, and notice what is there for you to notice now....
12) What do you notice now?
13) You might wish to allow some time for this to take its shape...
14) You might wish to notice it, with or without words...
b) When you are already in an opened state, and you wish to contain it before deepening.
Already open? Contain before you deepen

This can be used after the use of loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, severe grief, beautiful music, prayer, intense erotic energy, exhaustion, witnessing something of immense beauty, or any other activity which has opened you already, and which you wish to direct and stabilise before deepening.
The state is already opened, you merely need to aim and stabilise it.

Begin by looking around the room, grounding yourself in a sense of where and when you are. Feel your body in the chair or on the floor, and press your thumbs firmly into the first joint of your index fingers, focussing your attention on the physical sensation of friction between the skin of the two fingers.
Affirm to yourself that you will only allow in what you can integrate, and that your body is safe, and that you are an adult, not an inner child.
Once you have done this, choose one of the following:
Affirm: "I will only allow in the next useful piece of truth, symbol, feeling, question, or action, in digestible quantity."
When you find yourself falling into mental spaces and you want to remain in the physical world:
Stay awake when your mind likes to escape
Sit up straight, open your eyes, feel your feet, and breathe naturally.
Affirm: "I will not go away. I will come here instead."
Look at an object in front of you, and feel your spine.
Ask: "Am I receiving guidance in this daydream, digesting an emotional experience, or simply escaping from the present?"

Affirm: "If I am receiving guidance, please bring it to me in the form of actions I can take. If I am escaping, please bring me back gently into the present, and show me what I need to see about what I am avoiding."

If sitting still makes you sleepy, diffuse, or escape, create a hypnosis which increases alertness. Try keeping your eyes open, and performing a small movement (such as pressing your forefinger and thumb together and releasing them) repeatedly, focussing on increasing alertness and clarity with each repetition. Then stop performing the movement deliberately, and notice whether there is a natural continuation of the movement or not.

Affirm: "I will keep my eyes open, press my thumb and forefinger together, and release them, and increase my clarity with each repetition. Once more. And now I will stop deliberately moving my fingers, and notice what occurs in the first second after my deliberate movement has ceased. Is there an echo? Is there nothing? I will sit up straight, and work at this level."
The two-hand induction

Two-hand induction: Place one hand on your heart and the other on your solar plexis. Associate the hand on your heart with your Nurturer, and the one on your solar plexis with your vulnerable child. Breathe in and out gently while you say (mantra-style) “Love above. Child below. Adult present.” Or, “I send love to the child below. I receive signal from the child below. I send love to the child below. I receive signal from the child below.” etc.
Sleep induction

Using this to induce sleep: The difference between sleep induction and induction for inner work is that for inner work you will need to come back to Adult so that you can write things down, and act on them. For sleep, you don’t want to wake your Analytic mind up. You want revelation to take a backseat. So you can say to yourself “Analysis, you can go off duty now. You don’t need to reveal anything to me. You can wait until tomorrow to do that. Now is a time for rest.” For a sleep hypnosis induction to use as you go to bed, check out the sleep playlist on my Nimja page.
Optional fractionation: practice coming back

If you want to use fractionation to deepen trance, you can say to yourself “When I open my eyes, I will come back to ordinary awareness, and I can choose to stop this induction process and go back to what I was doing. If I want to deepen my trance, and continue with the induction, I will close or soften my eyes, and my trance will deepen. I can choose to stop at either point.”
Deepening, if useful

If you want to deepen your trance, you can say to yourself “If it’s useful to me, I will begin to feel more focused and absorbed in this process. If it’s not useful to me, I will remain just as awake as I am right now.” Imagine entering a special place in your imagination. You can decide ahead of time what this place is. It might be a room inside your heart, or a beautiful garden, or a temple. It could be sitting by a fire with your Protector nearby. It can be the side of a beautiful clear lake. It can be a specific chair where your Adult is waiting for you to come talk with him or her. Just pick one place, and stick with it. When you’re ready to start the inner work, you can ask yourself “Who or what needs to talk with me first?”
Optional trance depth check

If you want to check if you’re in a deep enough trance to proceed, you can say to yourself “As I wait for the right person or part to talk with me, I give up all responsibility for making things happen. If it’s useful to me, my subconscious wisdom may allow one of my fingers to begin twitching, or pulsing, or lifting on its own, or warming, or tingling, or some other subtle sensation, when the time is right for me to meet with whomever needs to meet with me inside. I will not force this sensation to appear. I will not fake it. I will just wait, with love.” etc. Some people’s fingers start twitching, some people’s hands start warming, some people’s breathing changes, some people experience nothing. You’re not doing it “right” or “wrong”. You’re either listening, or you’re not.
A shortcut back into hypnosis

Shortcut for hypnosis: Important: make sure you know how to do an induction and how to come out of hypnosis entirely before you learn how to set up a shortcut for getting hypnotized quickly. My dad has a mudra (hand sign) for relaxing. He brings two fingers together like you’re making an “okay” sign. He used to use it to relax while driving. Don’t do that. Keeping those two things separate is very important.

Pick a word or phrase (and, optionally, a hand gesture). When you’re already in a good, receptive hypnotic state (NOT at the peak of an emotional state, NOT in child state, NOT in the middle of a traumatic scene, etc.) say to yourself “From now on, when I deliberately use this [word or phrase (and gesture if applicable)], at a time and place that’s appropriate for inner work, I will enter this same state.” etc. Then come out of hypnosis entirely. The next time you want to do inner work, begin the process deliberately, and use your new shortcut. Over time, you can gradually shorten your longer induction until you’re using only the shortcut. If the shortcut doesn’t work on a given occasion, go back to using the longer induction. There’s no “magic number” of times you need to use the shortcut. It doesn’t need to get you into a deep trance in a second, or make you feel a particular sensation.

Check in with yourself to see if this shortcut is useful. Does it only get you into hypnosis when you deliberately want to use it? Can you change direction and come out of hypnosis when you want to? The answer to all these questions should be yes. If it gets you into a trance when you don’t want to go into a trance (someone else is narrating a scene, your phone notifies you of something, you overhear someone saying it, etc.), that’s not useful. How quickly you can get into a trance does not determine what you’re able to do with yourself, so don’t push for that.
Do not attempt to learn, or use, this technique while driving or doing anything that requires you to be actively paying attention.

If you ever want to cancel this shortcut, just stop rehearsing it. If you have a recording of it, don’t use the recording with the shortcut in it anymore. If it’s on an app, make sure it’s not in the active instructions. Just go back to using your regular induction. Like learning the shortcut, saying something to cancel the shortcut doesn’t mean it’s gone. If you find that you’re still responding to the shortcut when you don’t want to, or if it’s making you disoriented, ask for help from someone qualified. If you want to keep the shortcut for future use, just make sure that you’re coming entirely out of your altered state of consciousness when you finish your session.
